newsitem.title: UK: IPE announces gas oil contract review.
newsitem.headline: IPE announces gas oil contract review.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) announced on Thursday it had appointed energy consultant Sally Clubley to carry out an independent review of its gas oil contract following what it called recent strains.
An IPE statement said it expected the review to be completed by mid-March and anticipated Clubley would look at the way similar contracts were handled in the United States.

"The contract, while remaining liquid and successful, has been subjected to a number of strains in recent months, particularly as far as the delivery process is concerned," IPE chief executive Lynton Jones said.

"The IPE is convinced for the contract to continue to be successful, it is important that the contract specifications and the procedures governing delivery are in line with current practice in the physical market, are as robust as possible and command the support and confidence of the market place," he added.
The IPE added that in the event that Clubley recommended any changes, it expected to introduce such changes before the end of 1997.

The IPE statement made no mention of a showdown over the delivery of the November gas oil contract between AIC and Cargill that triggered widespread criticism by European oil traders of the conduct of the the continent's main winter oil market.
